sources.entry: Stringz - A lightweight and powerful editor for localizing iOS, macOS, tvOS, and watchOS applications.

summary.one_liner: Stringz is a lightweight macOS editor for managing localization strings across Xcode projects for iOS, macOS, tvOS, and watchOS apps.
summary.what_it_does: Stringz opens an Xcode project (.xcodeproj), automatically finds localizable files, and lists them in a sidebar. Translations are shown side by side in a table, with missing values highlighted and duplicate values flagged. It supports .strings, .storyboard, .xib, and .plist files, and can import strings from storyboard and xib files. Users can add, delete, and update strings, add new languages, and localize unlocalized files. The app includes undo/redo (Ctrl+Z), an autosave option that can be disabled in preferences, and preferences for importing and exporting localizable files.
use_cases: Translating an iOS app's strings into other languages
Localizing Info.plist app names and permission descriptions
Finding missing translations in an Xcode project
Importing strings from storyboards and xib files
Adding a new language to an existing Xcode app
how_to_run: Or download the app from the releases page of the repository
Open Stringz and select your Xcode project (.xcodeproj)
Select a localizable file from the sidebar to view and edit its strings
notable: Imports strings directly from storyboard and xib files, matching element IDs automatically
Side-by-side translation table that highlights missing values
Autosave can be turned off so Xcode does not reload on every edit
caveats: README does not state platform requirements beyond macOS focus; Xcode project required
Motivation section is empty in the README
No explicit license named in the README
